note: ADR-0222. Each case is one framed line and the message it must parse to. Both the C++ and Go implementations run this file; that is what stops them drifting.

cases.rationale: params is optional and absent means empty, so a caller never has to send a placeholder object.
A method with no id is fire and forget; the absence of id is the whole distinction, so it must not be inferred from the method name.
Raw paths travel base64 because JSON strings must be valid UTF-8 and paths are bytes.
A void operation still answers. Null result is present-and-empty, not absent, and must not be confused with an error.
code is machine-readable and stable; message is human text clients must not parse; context carries what the code cannot say.
Only the code is required, so an engine is never forced to invent prose to report a failure.
Events carry no id. They are not ordered against responses, so a client reconciles on state rather than sequence.
Job progress is an event stream, so a running job occupies no request slot -- the answer to ADR-0219's cover scan starving the control path.
Framing is one object per line. A newline inside a frame means the boundary was already lost, so it is refused rather than parsed as the first message.
An unparseable line is reported, never silently dropped.
Every message is an object; an array has no shape to dispatch on.
Without method, result, error or event there is nothing to do with the message.
A response is one or the other. Accepting both would let a sender express success and failure at once.
An event is unsolicited by definition; an id would imply it answers something.
A response with no id cannot be matched to a request, which defeats multiplexing.
Ids are positive so that zero stays available as an unmistakable not-a-request sentinel in implementations.
Coercing a scalar into an object hides a caller's mistake until it surfaces as a missing field.

raw_path_cases.rationale: The ordinary case, and the padding boundary for a 13 byte input.
Valid UTF-8 survives the round trip unchanged; 18 bytes needs no padding.
A raw path is bytes, not text. 0xff is not valid UTF-8 and could not appear in a JSON string, which is why paths are encoded at all.
An empty path encodes to nothing rather than to padding.
Two padding characters, the shortest non-empty encoding.

error_code_cases.rationale: Reported when a job or request stopped because it was asked to, which a client must be able to tell from a failure.
The caller sent something the engine cannot act on; retrying unchanged will not help.
The named thing does not exist. Distinct from an empty result, which is a success.
The operation collided with concurrent state, such as a saved search edited under a stale revision.
Also the answer to an unknown method, so a client talking to an older engine learns that rather than waiting forever.
A bound was hit -- request queue capacity, album grouping budget -- rather than something being wrong.
The filesystem refused. Usually transient and usually worth surfacing verbatim to the user.
A decoder, tag library or output device failed below the engine.
The catalogue or workspace store failed, which is not the user's doing and not retryable by them.
Something the engine believed impossible. Also where an unknown code from a newer engine lands, so that added codes are not a breaking change.

dispatch_cases.rationale: A request always gets exactly one response. Leaving an unknown method unanswered would hang the caller.
Error context survives the boundary, so a client can say which entry failed without parsing the message text.
The ordinary path: params in, result out, id echoed.
